service.name: Client dinner and member event entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music for client dinners, member events and private clubs
service.description: Jazz duo and small ensembles for client dinners, member events and private clubs in Denver, played at conversation volume with sound sized to the venue.

faqs.q: How loud is a jazz duo during dinner?
faqs.a: Dinner and cocktail sets run 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, a level you can talk across without raising your voice. If your venue or club enforces a cap, give us the number at contract and the evening is built under it.

faqs.q: What does music for a client dinner cost?
faqs.a: A jazz trio or acoustic duo for a dinner runs {{market:us_dinner_band}} in this market, which is the figure to budget against. Signet does not publish prices: send the date, the venue and the guest count and you get our number for that evening. There is no overtime rate, so an added half hour costs what the earlier ones did.

faqs.q: Can you invoice against a purchase order?
faqs.a: Yes. We can be set up as a vendor, quote against a PO, and invoice net-30 on approval, with the purchase order number on one itemised invoice. The certificate of insurance naming your venue and the W-9 arrive in the same email as the contract, before anyone has to ask for them.

faqs.q: Does the music stop for toasts and remarks?
faqs.a: Yes, before the speaker reaches the microphone. A dedicated announcement microphone is live on its own channel from the end of sound check, so toasts, introductions and remarks get a working mic of their own rather than the singer's. Transitions are set against your run of show before the event.

faqs.q: How much space does the duo need?
faqs.a: An 8 by 6 foot corner, one dedicated 20-amp circuit, and a 60-minute load-in. No stage and no house sound system are required: sound sized to the venue is included at every size, and the footprint for every size up to quartet is published on the technical page.
